items.title: Kenny Burrell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Joe Morgan, his PR guy, one of his PR people was also standing. Joe was kind of a figure that kind of hung around 52nd street... I think I was talking to Joe... And so Joe introduces me to Duke Ellington

ctx.x: Okay, lets take a break and we’ll start the rest of the tape on that too but we’re going to go ahead and get as much as we can on this one. Kimery: And we are rolling.

Okay, now the question was, when did I first meet Duke Ellington. Alright, I don’t remember when I first met Duke Ellington. I’ll just say I think it was around ’59 I was kind of hanging around the, that club on 52nd street that Billy Taylor used to play all the time. The Lunt-something, the something, it was a restaurant, the trio was playing there all the time on 52nd street. It was a good restaurant, I can’t think of the name of it, I’m sure you can think of it. But I was there that night, kind of hanging…

around that time, or a later time. He liked a couple of my compositions his nephew had told me. Prior to that I hadn’t met him formally but I had certainly seen him on the stage many times. But there was a restaurant, like a coffee shop, up in Harlem near the club that I used to play on a regular basis. I used to play at this place called Bowman’s, as I mentioned, which became Branker’s, and on one block from there on St. Nicholas Avenue and 155th street was this coffee shop and we would got there after we…
